transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-30 15:00 PST
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Priya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Lee (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (CTO - Luminary), Maya Singh (Head of ML), Ravi Patel (Infra)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): quick cost-focused discovery, some numbers discussed, follow-ups on pricing and POC.

[00:00] Priya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I know it's a busy week. Quick intros?
[00:05] Ethan Cole: Yeah Ethan here CTO at Luminary, we run inference across hybrid clouds, main concern today is unit cost at scale and whether we go hosted or dedicate or private, gap is big.
[00:12] Maya Singh: Hi, Maya, head of ML. We're evaluating model infra because costs have spiked on our current provider during peak.
[00:16] Ravi Patel: Ravi infra, I care about VPC, KMS, and egress.
[00:20] Priya Patel: Great. Jonah from our SE team will run through technical levers we typically use to drive down per-token costs — batching, prefix/KV caching, quant profiles, and also the differences in hosted vs dedicated vs private pricing.
[00:31] Jonah Lee: Quick caveat — transcriptions may swap words. But ok, numbers I give are indicative. For hosted API at Redwood we typically start with a base generation price in the range of $0.0006 per token for our standard models, embeddings are separate, obviously. For dedicated reserved capacity you get a significant delta — effective per-token can drop to something like $0.00015-$0.0003 depending on utilization, batch size, and whether you use quantized variants.
[00:55] Ethan Cole: Wait you said 0.0006 for hosted, and dedicated down to 0.00015? That delta is huge. Is that comparing apples to apples?
[01:05] Jonah Lee: Good question. Hosted includes multi-tenant overhead, dynamic scaling, and convenience. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools; unit economics improve because you're amortizing the GPU and can push larger batches and more aggressive quantization. Also caching reduces token counts.
[01:18] Maya Singh: On caching — what are realistic savings for our use case? Our app does lots of chat with repeated system prompts and a lot of retrieved context.
[01:26] Jonah Lee: Prefix/KV caching commonly yields 20-60% token savings depending on hit rate. If you have repeated system prompts + retrieval that's high hit rate. Example: if 40% of tokens are repeated across requests, that directly reduces billed tokens on Redwood hosted when prefix caching is enabled. On dedicated/private you can also run aggressive KV cache policies.
[01:43] Ravi Patel: How does batching factor into cost? We worry about latency.
[01:47] Jonah Lee: Batching increases throughput and lowers cost per token by improving GPU utilization. For medium-latency scenarios (like 200-500ms tail), you can batch micro-batches and get 10-30% cost reduction. For higher throughput non-real-time jobs, batching can drop cost per token by 40%+. But there's a tradeoff with latency SLOs. We can set routing policies — low-latency traffic to dedicated low-concurrency nodes, background traffic to high-batch nodes.
[02:10] Ethan Cole: What about quantization? We care about quality, not just price.
[02:13] Jonah Lee: Quantization (8-bit, 4-bit) can reduce memory and cost. For many LLMs 8-bit yields minimal quality loss and gives cost savings maybe 15-30% on inference. 4-bit is more aggressive — sometimes 30-60% savings but you must validate quality on your prompt set. Redwood Optimize gives suggested quant profiles by workload.
[02:30] Maya Singh: Can you show a worked example? Say we run 100M tokens/month today. How do hosted vs dedicated cost compare roughly?
[02:37] Jonah Lee: Sure, rough back-of-envelope: Hosted at $0.0006/token -> $60,000/month for 100M tokens. Dedicated effective rate say $0.0002 -> $20,000/month plus reserved capacity fee (e.g., monthly commit for GPUs). Private/on-prem depends on capex+support but can be similar to dedicated once amortized. With caching 40% hit rate, tokens billed become 60M, so hosted -> $36k, dedicated -> $12k. Add quantization and batching you could get down further.
[03:05] Ethan Cole: Our budget for inference is ~$25k/mo initially, scaling later. So dedicated looks attractive if the committed cost aligns. How does commitment pricing work?
[03:14] Priya Patel: For Redwood Dedicated we do monthly or annual reserved capacity. You pick GPU pool size and commit. The more you commit the better the unit economics. We also support burst capacity so you don't need to overcommit for peaks. We can model a 6-month ramp in the pricing sheet.
[03:29] Ravi Patel: For private deployment, ie VPC or on-prem, what are the hidden costs — network, ops overhead?
[03:35] Jonah Lee: Private has additional ops and network costs; you manage the infra or we provide a packaged on-prem offering. KMS/HSM integration and SOC2 compliance adds to time-to-prod. Upfront is higher but per-token can be cheapest if utilisation is high. Also consider staff time.
[03:50] Maya Singh: We're also worried about procurement — procurement window is ~6-8 weeks for anything with enterprise contracts.
[03:56] Priya Patel: Noted. We can provide a pricing + SOW template and legal sheet to speed that up.
[04:02] Ethan Cole: Any other levers? For example, model selection — smaller models for some tasks?
[04:07] Jonah Lee: Absolutely. Right-size model to task. For short form classification or intent detection, smaller open models or quantized variants can be 5-10x cheaper than running a big generalist model. Redwood supports model cataloging and automatic routing so you can route cheap models for cheap tasks and large models for hard tasks.
[04:21] Ethan Cole: Does hosted support custom model pinning? Like pin to an exact weights set?
[04:24] Priya Patel: Yes, you can pin model versions in hosted and in dedicated/private. For strict reproducibility we recommend dedicated or private.
[04:31] Maya Singh: Any performance guarantees on hosted?
[04:34] Priya Patel: Hosted has SLAs for availability, but latency SLOs are better on Dedicated which can be backed by an SLA for tail latencies in enterprise contracts. We'll include specifics in the SLA doc.
[04:44] Ravi Patel: Security — SOC2, SSO, audit logs, key management — is that ready for enterprise?
[04:49] Priya Patel: Yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II; we integrate with SAML/SSO, role-based access, and you can use customer-managed KMS for Private. We'll share SOC2 and our security whitepaper.
[05:00] Maya Singh: For the POC benchmark — what's a reasonable test to estimate our costs?
[05:03] Jonah Lee: Provide 3-5 representative prompts and traffic mix (percentages of short/long responses). We'll run a short run across hosted and dedicated configs: single A100, single A10g, and a quantized dedicated node. We'll measure tokens billed, tail latency, and throughput. That will give you extrapolated monthly cost.
[05:20] Ethan Cole: Ok. Also curious about caching on hosted — do you charge for cached tokens?
[05:24] Jonah Lee: You only pay for tokens that are generated or retrieved beyond the cache hit; prefix/KV cache reduces billed tokens. There are edge cases with certain retrieval flows; Jonah: we document them.
[05:34] Priya Patel: Also worth noting we have Cedric (not on call) who handles finance modeling; we'll loop him in for the committed pricing.
[05:40] Maya Singh: Any concerns with model quality when using quantized weights and larger batches?
[05:44] Jonah Lee: Quality can be affected by quantization; batching itself doesn't change quality but can change latency. We'll run A/B on your prompt set. We recommend keeping a quality baseline and automatic regression alerts during POC.
[05:56] Ethan Cole: Procurement aside, timeline — we want a pilot in Jan, decision by end of Feb. Is that feasible?
[06:01] Priya Patel: Yes, we can scope a 2-week pilot in Jan, benchmark in week 1 and validate quality in week 2.
[06:07] Ravi Patel: For private deployment, we need to know minimal network egress and KMS footprint. We'll share network diagrams.
[06:12] Priya Patel: Please share diagrams; Jonah will review.
[06:15] Maya Singh: Any gotchas for billing when we do high-volume batching?
[06:19] Jonah Lee: Billing is based on tokens billed post-cache. If you batch multiple users into a single request we still bill the resulting tokens generated. So efficiency comes from reuse (caching) and smaller models for simpler tasks. Also for embeddings there's separate unit math.
[06:32] Ethan Cole: Competitor question — how are you different from OpenAI or Anthropic on cost?
[06:36] Priya Patel: Short answer — we focus on production economics and deployment flexibility. Our pricing is transparent and we provide dedicated/private modes for teams that need better economics or isolation. We also provide tooling (Optimize) to recommend batching and quantization.
[06:48] Maya Singh: They asked about audit logs retention — how long?
[06:51] Priya Patel: Default retention is 90 days for hosted, longer retention is an add-on. For dedicated/private you can configure retention to meet compliance.
[06:59] Ethan Cole: Ok good. Let's recap actions.
[07:02] Priya Patel: Recap — we'll send: pricing sheet and committed scenarios, SOC2 and security docs, POC plan + benchmark configs. Luminary to share prompts, traffic mix, and network diagrams. We'll set the POC kickoff first week of Jan.
[07:18] Maya Singh: Sounds good.
[07:19] Ravi Patel: Thanks everyone.
[07:20] Priya Patel: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
